<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/deferred-and-cross-request-state/">Deferred work and cross-request state</a><span class="nv-section-count">14</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Work that outlives the response but not the request, and the only way a value outlives the request that made it.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/deferred-and-cross-request-state/#after-response-outlives-the-connection"><code>Core\Task::afterResponse</code> runs after the request's own frame returns, still charged to the request tree</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from not defer more</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a than queueing</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/deferred-and-cross-request-state/#cross-request-state-is-explicit">A value outlives the request that made it only by being put into a named store</a><span <section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/">Persistent connections</a><span class="nv-section-count">11</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A WebSocket or an SSE stream is a root isolate with a loop in it, upgraded from a request that then ends.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-connection-is-a-root-isolate">A persistent connection is a root isolate, and the request that upgraded it ends</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped">An upgrade names compiled code — a file or a static method — and never a closure</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#an-upgrades-options-are-spawn-scripts">An upgrade's <code>args</code>, <code>limits</code>, <code>grants</code> and <code>on</code> are a spawned script's options as ordinary named arguments</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-connection-is-a-loop">Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop, and <code>receive()</code> answering <code>null</code> is what ends it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#receive-is-the-one-wait"><code>receive()</code> is the one wait, and it answers the peer or a subscribed topic, whichever arrives first</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-peer-frame-is-tainted">What a peer sent arrives <code>tainted</code>, and <code>Core\Validate</code> is the only way to launder it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection">A stream that ends with its response is a streaming response; one that outlives it is a connection isolate</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#two-doors-one-isolate"><code>Core\Socket</code> and <code>Core\Sse</code> are two hand-overs onto one isolate, and each reports the one it is missing</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#connection-bounds-are-finite">Every bound on an open connection is finite with nothing configured</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit">An open connection runs to completion on the code it started with, and an edit reaches only the next one</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/connections/#a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly">A shutdown or a reload closes a connection with a defined code after a drain, never with a reset</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/">The job queue</a><span class="nv-section-count">10</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Enqueue commits with your own write. Four members, at-least-once delivery, finite attempts, and a dead letter that is kept.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#enqueue-commits-with-your-write">A <code>push</code> on the queue's connection commits with the write that caused it, or neither happens</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#queue-four-members"><code>Core\Queue</code>'s four request-path members are each asked about a job or about a queue, never about a row number</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#a-tag-groups-jobs-and-a-key-dedupes-them">A <code>tag</code> names a group of jobs and a <code>key</code> admits one pending job, and they are two columns because they are opposites</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#a-job-names-a-file">A job names a script file, and its payload crosses as a copied value</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue">A job's budget and grants are recorded when it is enqueued, and narrowed from that context rather than widened</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#claiming-is-one-statement">A worker claims a job with one statement the database arbitrates, so a fleet needs no lease protocol</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#a-job-between-attempts-is-pending">A job between attempts is <code>Pending</code>, and there is no <code>Failed</code> state to ask about</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#delivery-is-at-least-once">Delivery is at-least-once, and idempotency is the job's own obligation</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept">Attempts are finite, backoff is exponential and jittered, and an exhausted job is kept rather than href="/docs/rules/concurrency/the-job-queue/#a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt">A job that exceeds its budget is a failed attempt, reported as that and retried like any other</a><span <section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/">Running a job</a><span class="nv-section-count">9</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">A job is a root isolate on a recorded budget. Which process runs it is configuration, and there is no pluggable driver.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose"><code>cancel</code> answers whether it won the race, and it changes the job's state rather than deleting the row</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded">A queue row is removed by <code>delete</code> or <code>purge</code>, never while claimed, and never dead-lettered or pending unless the call says so</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate">A job runs as a root isolate, and there is no second execution path</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#who-runs-a-job-is-configuration">Which process runs a job is configuration, and every spelling drives the identical isolate</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs"><code>nvs serve</code> runs the accept loop, the schedule ticker and the queue's workers in one process, and the drain stops all three</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers">A durable payload refuses <code>secret</code>, and a <code>tainted</code> value comes back <code>tainted</code></a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted">A <code>push</code> on a connection other than the queue's is not transactional, and is counted rather than assumed away</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/concurrency/running-a-job/#no-broker-and-no-driver-interface">There is no broker backend and no pluggable driver, because a driver makes transactional enqueue optional</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li></ol>
</section>
